summary: Feed s117_double is degraded for APM: 56.2% of TCP sessions are one-way (tool requires both directions) and 11.3% of packets are duplicates. APM cannot correlate request/response and will miscalculate latency/availability.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of many flows is reaching the APM. Most likely the packet broker is not aggregating both sides of the conversation to the same tool port, or TAP/SPAN coverage is incomplete on the return path / asymmetric routing is not being combined. 72 of 128 sessions affected.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs both directions to pair requests with responses and measure transaction latency. With one-way traffic it sees incomplete transactions, cannot compute response times, inflates error rates and misses performance degradations.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow (both TAPs/SPANs and both sides of asymmetric paths) to the same APM tool port so request/response pairs are complete.

findings.root_cause: 11.3% duplicate packets (181/1605) indicates the same packet is being delivered twice, typically from aggregating two SPANs/TAPs that see the same traffic without broker deduplication, or a loop/SPAN duplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will double-count transactions, skew latency and throughput metrics, waste its 10G capacity and storage, and can trigger false alerts on retransmits/errors even though payload inspection is not required.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication on feed s117_double to suppress identical packets arriving within a short window before forwarding to the APM.
